purpose: Single source of review questions for the OPS-04 review deck. One entry per question a worker could not settle by evidence; the producer appends here at merge time (docs/roles/PRODUCER.md step 5).

questions.question: Are callout marks (window-frame outlines and leaders over empty desktop) over a whole Microsoft screenshot acceptable?
Original: 'Project Explorer' (VB6 term) or VB4's 'Project window'? Lower priority: 'Form Designer' is also VB6 documentation wording for what VB4 material calls the form; keep it, or use e.g. 'Form'?

The narration over this visual (War/SCRIPT.md:135) says the form was 'in the center' as 'a blank gray window' and the code window was 'behind all of it'. In the only accepted VB4 capture the form is centre-left, it is a populated Microsoft sample (LoanSheet), and the Code window is open in front of the form. Toolbox-left and properties-right match. Keep the narration as a general description of the IDE (possibly with 'behind' read as 'the code behind the form'), soften it (for example 'and a code window where you wrote your actual BASIC'), or ask the edit to hold on the clean screenshot during that sentence? No script edit was made and the art is unchanged.

No credit is burned into any variant, because HIST-02's proposed credit ('... Used with permission from Microsoft.') must not be used before the rights basis is decided. If Microsoft's screenshot permission is the chosen basis, where should the required statement go: video description, end credits, or on screen? Layout facts for the decision (no art changed): side-by-side leaves an empty dark area below the clean screenshot inside the safe area (about x 120-935, y 770-1008), so an on-screen line would fit there without re-layout; five-callouts and clean-workspace at 1.5x have no room inside the safe area below the screenshot (an on-screen line would need the image reduced to about 1.44x and a re-render).

The cue says 'Side-by-side'. Is cut/dissolve between two full-frame stills acceptable, or is a split-screen wanted?

May the video use this 1995 Borland International marketing screenshot of the Delphi 1.0 IDE — now acquired byte-exact from the Wayback Machine, Borland copyright, no licence found, and covered by a site notice prohibiting reproduction for redistribution — under an editorial/commentary rationale, with the proposed credit 'Borland International, Inc. — Delphi 1.0 Reviewer's Guide (1995), via the Internet Archive Wayback Machine'? Or must HIST-12 stay blocked for release, or be replaced by a clearly labelled original reconstruction (a separate ticket decision)? No agent clearance has been given.

It is presented at an exact 3x integer upscale (1332x846) on a matte rather than stretched to fill 1920x1080, so it does not fill the frame and shows visible period pixel structure. Confirm that this presentation is acceptable for the section-13 cutaway, or ask for a different treatment (for example a tighter reversible crop on the Object Inspector and code window). Screen text stays legible at 720p, which was checked.
